actual.value:
**Output 1. Capacity of ISPG staff has been strengthened on a technical level, with regard to skills and knowledge on sustainable low-cost development of shallow groundwater from NBS for multiple-use**
All the courses in the Division of Agriculture at ISPG were developed to address community-oriented needs and they are all water dependent. Based in a semi-arid region with climate variability, it is a challenge for economic and social development of local communities. This is why it was important for the TMT+ to be all inclusive in targeting ISPG staff to be trained. The first phase involved training of trainers and this was done in four parts (ToT 1 – 4). By the end of the first phase, 18 individuals with various backgrounds had been trained (Environmental Engineering, Irrigation Engineering, Hydraulics Engineering, Water Resources Management, Integrate Water and Soil Management, Water and Wastewater Engineering, Hydrogeology and Groundwater Resources, Agricultural Engineering, Horticulture, Food Science and Technology, Sustainable Aquaculture, Geosciences, GIS and Mapping). Of the staff trained, 35% were women.
**Output 2. ISPG has become a centre of excellence in this field, having added NBS expertise to its regular curriculum, but also having the capacity to train other public and private water professionals in charge of rural development**
The TMT+ enriched ISPG’s knowledge on NBS sustainable exploration and exploitation and added much needed skills and equipment for the institution to become a centre of excellence in the field. ISPG has managed to train 42 professionals from public and private institutions as well as 10 students doing their research directly in the project. Regarding the scope, the trainings were given to participants from three hydrological basins (Limpopo, Save and Zambezi River Basins) in the Southern and Central parts of Mozambique. Additional skills and knowledge of 3 ISPG staff members were developed in support of their PhD studies, through 3 short courses: Groundwater Data Collection and Interpretation, Groundwater Modelling and Decentralized Water Supply and Sanitation.
The expertise gained has ensured that this groundwater exploration for multiple use services is included in the Agricultural Hydraulics and Rural Water Engineering course curriculum as well as practical field lessons. The involvement of students has been fundamental for further development of knowledge in the field through research. A total number of 10 BSc theses in Agricultural Hydraulics and Rural Water Engineering were developed. These were direct and indirect benefits from the NBS expertise from the institution.
A comprehensive online course ([https://ocw.un-ihe.org/course/view.php?id=247&sesskey=JzpP4XDvtC](https://ocw.un-ihe.org/course/view.php?id=247&sesskey=JzpP4XDvtC), currently being subtitled in Portuguese) and three short courses on the low-cost development of shallow groundwater from NBS for multiple use have been developed to ensure further uptake of the knowledge.
**Output 3. Participants from other organizations in water supply and agriculture (knowledge institutes, governmental bodies, associations, private sector, NGOs) are trained on low-cost development of shallow groundwater from NBS**
Two Tailor Made Trainings were carried out in November 2022 and March 2023, where ISPG staff trained 42 participants from governmental bodies, knowledge institutes, farmer groups, private water providers:
· A total of 32 participants were from the governmental bodies in the 14 districts of Gaza province (15 from District Services for Planning and Infrastructure (SDPI); 14 from District Services for Economic Activities (SDAE); 1 from the Regional Water Authority for the Southern Region (ARA-Sul) and 3 from the Provincial Directorate for Public Works, Housing and Water Resources (DPOP)).
· 3 participants were from knowledge institutions (Higher Polytechnic Institute of Manica (ISPM), Higher Polytechnic Institute of Tete (ISPT) and Higher Polytechnic Institute of Songo (ISPS)).
· 6 participants were farmers (individual and association representative).
· 1 participant was a private water provider.
**Output 4. Through the obtained knowledge and skills participants are able to promote and support the implementation of local or regional water supply and agricultural programmes, e.g. within governmental or private initiatives.**
There has been knowledge and skills implementation by staff in other projects. ISPG was a partner in the implementation of the Farmer-led Smallholder Irrigation in Mozambique (FASIMO) headed by the University of Eduardo Mondlane (UEM), with International Development Research Centre Canada (IDRC), Australian Centre for international Agricultural Research (ACIAR), and the National Irrigation Institute (INIR). Using the low-cost technology, staff drilled monitoring boreholes in irrigation schemes together with students doing their field work at FASIMO. Another project sponsored by the Dutch government, Community Empowerment through Sustainable Resource Use and Agricultural Value Chain Development in the Limpopo Basin (CES-RURAL) also benefited from skills and knowledge gained.
Low cost drilling companies were formed and trained by PRACTICA Foundation as part of a spinoff from NBS development. The companies are comprised of trained staff as well as undergraduates.
**Output 5. ISPG will have strengthened its network and partnerships on a regional and national level**
After this TMT+, ISPG has managed to strengthen its relation with a number of organisations and also work with new ones. ISPG has worked with IHE Delft in previous projects, the partnership has been cemented and there will be lots of opportunities for both institutions in the future. Beside IHE Delft, PRACTICA Foundation has also improved its relations with ISPG. Outside of this project, PRACTICA and ISPG trained and formed small manual drilling companies and are working together in the province to promote NBS exploitation for small scale farmers. For the first time, ISPG has worked with IRC creating yet another partner regionally.
On a national level, ISPG has spread its roots in all the districts of Gaza Province with the positive interaction with District Services for Planning and Infrastructure (SDPI) and District Services for Economic Activities (SDAE). The Provincial Directorate for Public Works, Housing and Water Resources (DPOP) was very fundamental in bringing all the districts together and is a very collaborative institution. This paves way for future alliances and projects to be done in the province.
ISPG also has a lot to benefit from ISPM, ISPT, ISPS, and CFPAS, with all being educational institutions. These partnerships are still being cemented and their inclusion in this TMT+ has been very beneficial for all parties. Similarly, FIPAG is also an important partner for ISPG, especially since their laboratory is better equipped than ISPG’s and having such a partner is essential. Also, during the four-year undergraduate programs at ISPG, students are required to do work related learning and can be attached in any of these organisations and institutions. This also applies for their bachelor’s projects.
Because of the NBS expertise, the Limpopo Watercourse Commission (LIMCOM) has identified ISPG as an important stakeholder in the Limpopo River Basin. LIMCOM is a commission dedicated to the coordination of the Limpopo River Basin transboundary management.
